The file mocks `SafeReact` to test the id fallback of React 17. Vue has `useId` in each version that the package supports.

`OTPField.test.ts` tests the code, `v-model` and the change, invalid and complete events, the form input and its validity, `autoSubmit`, the reset, the field, the names, the tab stop and the order of the slots, with the native elements of the parts. `OTPField.hydration.test.ts` tests the server HTML.
`OTPField.test.ts` tests the attributes of a slot, typed text, paste, the keys, Enter, the focus, the click, the composition and the fill of a slot, with a real keyboard and pointer in each browser.
`OTPField.android.test.ts` mocks the platform and tests the same composition.
`code.test.ts` tests each case of the file on the functions of `code.ts`, and the flag of refused characters.
`OTPField.spec.tsx` tests the namespace types, the required `length`, and the `event` of the details by `reason`.
`OTPField.spec.tsx` tests that a slot takes the attributes of an input and no `index`. The slot has no `render` slot: the `element` slot gives its props.

exceptions.title: allows a composed focus handler to prevent internal focus state
exceptions.reason: The case tests the focused state of the field, which is cut. CSS selects `:focus` and `:focus-within` (rule 8.15).

exceptions.title: allows a composed blur handler to preserve internal focus state
exceptions.reason: The case tests the focused state of the field, which is cut. CSS selects `:focus` and `:focus-within` (rule 8.15).

exceptions.title: allows a composed mousedown handler to prevent focus
exceptions.reason: `event.preventDefault()` on a native listener has its native meaning only, so a listener of the developer does not stop the code of the part (rule 8.7).

exceptions.title: stops propagation when ArrowDown moves focus to the empty end slot
exceptions.reason: The slot calls `preventDefault()` for a key that it handles, and the event reaches an ancestor, as from a native input. A composite around the field acts only on its own items.

exceptions.title: does not reselect the final slot when typing the same character
exceptions.reason: The case counts the calls of `select()`. The case of the key of the selected character tests what the user sees: the focus moves, and the code does not change.

exceptions.title: leaves vertical arrow navigation unhandled in disabled mode
exceptions.reason: A disabled input gets no key from a user.

exceptions.title: warns in development when clipboard text cannot be read during paste handling
exceptions.reason: A `paste` event of a browser has `clipboardData`, and its text can always be read.

exceptions.title: ignores a paste event when clipboard text is unavailable
exceptions.reason: A `paste` event of a browser has `clipboardData`, and its text can always be read.

exceptions.title: adds disabled and readonly state attributes to each slot
exceptions.reason: A slot has no `data-disabled` and no `data-readonly`: CSS selects `:disabled` and `:read-only` on the same input (rule 8.15).

exceptions.title: applies a native label to every slot
exceptions.reason: A `<label for>` names the first input only, as in HTML. `aria-labelledby` on the root names the group, and a `Field.Label` names the group and each input.

exceptions.title: keeps the shared label on the first slot even if an aria-label is provided
exceptions.reason: The `aria-label` of the developer wins on each slot, the first one too, and the part gives no warning (rule 8.2).

exceptions.title: warns when aria-label is provided on the first slot without an associated label
exceptions.reason: The `aria-label` of the developer wins on each slot, the first one too, and the part gives no warning (rule 8.2).

exceptions.title: does not warn for a first-slot aria-label when a native label is associated
exceptions.reason: The `aria-label` of the developer wins on each slot, the first one too, and the part gives no warning (rule 8.2).

exceptions.title: does not warn for a first-slot aria-label when Field.Label is associated
exceptions.reason: The `aria-label` of the developer wins on each slot, the first one too, and the part gives no warning (rule 8.2).

exceptions.title: applies single-character validation to each visible slot
exceptions.reason: A slot accepts only the characters of the type, so a `pattern` on a slot can never fail. The form input has the `pattern` of a whole code.

exceptions.title: omits the hidden validation pattern when set to `none`
exceptions.reason: The form input of the type `none` has the pattern `.{length}`, so an incomplete code fails the native validation of each type (rule 8.11).

exceptions.title: updates standalone filled and focused state on the root
exceptions.reason: The case asserts the focused state of the root, which is cut (rule 8.15). The cases of the filled state test `data-filled`.

exceptions.title: renders password slot inputs when enabled
exceptions.reason: `mask` is cut. `type="password"` on each `OTPField.Input` is the native attribute on the element that it changes.

exceptions.title: redirects hidden validation input focus to the first visible slot
exceptions.reason: The form input gives the focus to the end slot: the first empty slot, where the user types next. For an empty code it is the first slot.

exceptions.reason: A fill of the form input moves the focus only when the field has it, so a fill does not take the focus from another control (WCAG 3.2.2).

exceptions.title: keeps the completed value when the owning form has no requestSubmit method
exceptions.reason: `requestSubmit()` is Baseline Widely available, so each form has it.

exceptions.title: does not call flushSync inside a layout effect when auto-submitting a Base UI Form
exceptions.reason: The case tests `flushSync` of React in a layout effect. Vue has neither.

exceptions.title: blocks invalid Base UI Form auto-submit without calling flushSync inside a layout effect
exceptions.reason: The case tests `flushSync` of React. The case of a `Form` that blocks the submit tests the blocked submit and the focus.

`v-model` replaces `value` and `onValueChange`. `autocomplete`, `inputmode` and `readonly` replace `autoComplete`, `inputMode` and `readOnly`, also in the state (rule 8.2). `mask` is cut: `type="password"` on each `OTPField.Input` is the native attribute on the element that it changes. The state has no `focused`, and the group has no `data-focused`: CSS selects `:focus-within` (rule 8.15). The details of a change have no `allowPropagation`, `isPropagationAllowed` or `trigger`: the part stops no event, and `details.event.target` is the element (rule 8.6). `class`, `style` and the `element` slot replace `className`, `style` and `render`.

The input has no props: the attributes of an input type it, so the part has no props type. It has no `data-disabled`, `data-readonly`, `data-required`, `data-invalid` and `data-focused`: CSS selects `:disabled`, `:read-only`, `:required`, `[aria-invalid="true"]` and `:focus` on the same input (rule 8.15). `readonly` replaces `readOnly` in the state, and the state has no `focused`. `class`, `style` and the `element` slot replace `className`, `style` and `render`.
The parts write the attribute names that the docs list, and CSS selects them as text. The family has no namespace of constants (rule 8.10).

The part is `Separator`. The part writes `aria-orientation`, which the role `separator` takes, so CSS selects `[aria-orientation='vertical']` and the part writes no `data-orientation` (rule 8.15). The family has no namespace of constants (rule 8.10).

A slot shows its character, and gives the root its text, its keys and its focus.
